title: Fpqc effectivity for separated flat group schemes over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $F$ be a contravariant functor from $S$-schemes to groups, with no commutativity assumption, whose underlying set-valued functor is an fpqc sheaf: for every fpqc covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], the map $F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)$ identifies $F(U)$ with the equalizer of the two restriction maps to $\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\times_U U_j)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose there is an fpqc morphism of schemes $p:T\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that the restriction $F_T$ to $T$-schemes is represented, as a group sheaf, by a separated flat group scheme $P\to T$ locally of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the group identities, and separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $F$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. Neither $P$ nor its generic fibre is required to be quasi-compact; smoothness and an affine-neighbourhood condition are not hypotheses.

source.place: Anantharaman, Schemas en groupes, espaces homogenes et espaces algebriques sur une base de dimension 1, Memoires SMF 33 (1973), Theorem 4.A, printed p.53, flat case over a trait; proof 4.2 Steps 4-6, printed pp.57-62, including the reduction from local finite presentation to finite-presentation open pieces. Local archive WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf Corrected after return b9ec6f96471: the sheaf hypothesis is fpqc, not merely fppf; the stronger topology is necessary for descent along the specified fpqc cover.

proof.text: Apply the finite-component-open lemma to the given $F,p,P$. Obtain the open subgroup $H$ and the covering open subfunctors $U_a$, with $H_T$ and $(U_a)_T$ flat separated and of finite presentation. Keep its integral fpqc covers $B_a\to S$ with finite underlying fibres, where $B_a$ is the semi-trait obtained by normalization in a finite, possibly ramified field extension, and the finite almost homogeneous decompositions over them. No total quasi-compactness of $P$ is inferred.

source.place: 4.2 Step 5, Lemma 4.2.4 and following action argument, printed pp.59-61; generic-only extension using ramified normalization is stated in the cited component lemma (E2 repair).

proof.text: First, $H$, every $U_a$ and their restrictions to schemes over any $S$-scheme are fpqc sheaves: given an fpqc covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ and compatible sections $s_i$ of the open subfunctor, they glue to a unique $s\in F(V)$ by the sheaf property of $F$; the open subscheme of $V$ over which $s$ lies in the subfunctor contains the image of every $V_i$, and these images cover $V$, so it is $V$. Apply the normalization-model lemma to the fpqc sheaf $H$, using the finite-presentation model $H_T$ from step 1. It gives an integral fpqc normalization $S_L\to S$ with finite underlying fibres and a flat separated finite-presentation scheme $N$ representing $H_{S_L}$. Its group law is represented by scheme maps: multiply the universal points on $N\times_{S_L}N$ to define multiplication, use the identity on $S_L$, and invert the universal point on $N$; the representing bijections turn the group identities into the corresponding diagram equalities. Under left translation $N$ is homogeneous under itself: the inverse to $(g,x)\mapsto(gx,x)$ is $(y,x)\mapsto(yx^{-1},x)$. The affine-neighbourhood lemma with $G=X=N$ therefore gives (FA). Since $S_L$ is Noetherian and $N$ is of finite presentation, the locally-Noetherian lemma makes $N$ locally Noetherian. The integral fpqc affine-descent lemma now represents $H$ by a flat separated finite-presentation $S$-scheme with (FA); its model and cover hypotheses are precisely those just obtained.

source.place: 4.2 Step 4, printed p.57, applied to the finite-presentation open subgroup of Step 5.

proof.text: Fix $a$. By step 1, $B_a\to S$ is an integral fpqc cover with finite underlying fibres, and $B_a$ is a Noetherian semi-trait. The group $H_{B_a}$ is a scheme by step 2, flat and separated by the cited base-change lemmas, and of finite type by the cited finite-type base-change lemma (finite presentation includes finite type). Its action on $(U_a)_{B_a}$ is the action of step 1. This uses no etaleness of $B_a\to S$.

source.place: 4.2 Step 6, printed p.61, with the cited component lemma allowing ramified normalization covers for generic-only pieces.

proof.text: Put $B=B_a$ and apply the normalization-model lemma to $(U_a)_B$. Pull back the original fpqc cover and its model; the flat/separated base-change lemmas and clause (3) of qcqs-morphism permanence retain flatness, separatedness and finite presentation. Obtain an integral fpqc normalization $V\to B$ with finite fibres and a flat separated finite-presentation scheme $X$ representing $(U_a)_V$. The acting group $H_V$ is a flat separated finite-type scheme by the same three base-change lemmas as step 3. The finite homogeneous open cover of step 1 pulls back to $X$: its local solutions to $h x=y$ pull back along every test-scheme map, so the action remains almost homogeneous over $V$. Apply the affine-neighbourhood lemma to $H_V$ acting on $X$ to get (FA). The locally-Noetherian lemma applies to $X/V$ since $V$ is Noetherian and $X$ is of finite presentation. Apply the integral fpqc affine-descent lemma to $V\to B$ to represent $(U_a)_B$ by a flat separated finite-presentation scheme with (FA).

source.place: 4.2 Steps 4 and 6, printed pp.57 and 61; apply the almost homogeneous argument to each open piece.

proof.text: Apply integral fpqc affine descent once more, now to the sheaf $U_a$ and $B_a\to S$. Its scheme over $B_a$ has (FA) by step 4 and is locally Noetherian by the cited locally-Noetherian lemma (it is of finite presentation over the Noetherian scheme $B_a$). Its original fpqc model is the finite-presentation scheme $(U_a)_T$ of step 1. Thus $U_a$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. This argument applies independently to every $a$; it needs no uniform finite cover for all pieces.

source.place: 4.2 Step 6, printed p.61, using the general integral fpqc descent criterion on each normalization cover; etaleness is not needed.

proof.text: The underlying functor of $F$ is a Zariski sheaf: every Zariski open covering is fpqc, so its matching sections glue uniquely by the assumed equalizer condition. Steps 1 and 5 supply a set-indexed family of representable subfunctors $U_a\subseteq F$, whose inclusions are representable open immersions and which covers on every scheme test. All clauses of the cited representability criterion hold. It gives an $S$-scheme representing $F$.

source.place: Tag 01JJ, schemes.tex lemma-glue-functors; Anantharaman 4.2 Step 6, printed p.61.

The component-opens node now takes B_a = Spec of the integral closure of R in a finite, possibly ramified extension. Krull–Akizuki, integrality, lying over and torsion-freeness make this an integral, surjective, flat, qc cover with finite fibres by a Noetherian normal semi-trait; this needs neither excellence nor finiteness over R. The returned Z²/K(√π) example now satisfies the statement (L⊗L = L×L gives singleton pieces).
